mechanism_narrative: The sharp weekly recovery in WORKPLACES from -59.0 to -32.0 signals a return-to-office rebound that should raise weekday retail and recreation visits with a 2-4 week lag. If commuting continues to normalize, RETAIL_REC will be less negative than in the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -59.0 at t-2w to -32.0 at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed deeply negative near -56
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -40 and RETAIL_REC remains more negative than the previous four-week mean over the next 28 days, reject this mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When residential time remains elevated above baseline, discretionary shopping is postponed and local trips substitute for mall and dining outings, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week. The current high RESIDENTIAL level should therefore suppress retail mobility while stay-at-home behavior persists.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 13.4 at t-2w, 14.1 at t-1w, and 12.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls back below 10 while RETAIL_REC still declines further over the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates households are resuming short outside trips without restoring broader discretionary outings. That mix should pull retail-and-recreation down over the next two weeks because essential errands and park visits absorb mobility that would otherwise go to retail venues.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive near 1.9 to 10.7 while PARKS moved from -5.3 to 21.6 and then back to -8.9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rise together but RETAIL_REC becomes less negative over the next 14 days, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently depressed TRANSIT series below -50 implies reduced access to dense commercial areas and weaker spontaneous shopping trips, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average for the next four weeks. The effect is strongest while transit remains constrained rather than merely volatile.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 for at least three consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -48.7, -56.4, -56.4, and -55.9 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -50 but RETAIL_REC rises above the prior four-week mean within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap between rising RESIDENTIAL and falling WORKPLACES indicates more time spent at home and fewer work-linked retail trips. Over the next month, that substitution should reduce retail-and-recreation mobility relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above 12 while WORKPLACES improved but remained deeply negative, creating a persistent home-work split
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES remains below -25 but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the prior 28 days, reject this claim.

mechanism_narrative: A brief spike in PARKS mobility followed by a reversal indicates weather- or calendar-driven outdoor substitution rather than durable reopening. That pattern should lift retail only for one week at most; by the four-week window, RETAIL_REC should be lower than the previous month as the park impulse fades.
candidate_trigger: PARKS jumps above 15 and then falls back below 5 the following week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -5.3 at t-3w to 21.6 at t-2w, then dropped to 3.4 and -8.9
failure_condition: If a PARKS spike above 15 is followed by sustained retail improvement over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays severely depressed while WORKPLACES rebounds, the mix implies selective commuting by a smaller employed core rather than broad consumer reopening. In that case, retail visitation should improve only after a two-week delay and remain weaker than baseline, because the transport bottleneck limits shopping access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -55 while WORKPLACES improves by at least 15 points from its recent trough
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT hovered near -56 while WORKPLACES rebounded from -59.0 to -32.0
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES improves while TRANSIT stays below -55 and RETAIL_REC rises above the prior four-week mean within two weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent deterioration in RETAIL_REC and only modest recovery in GROCERY_PHARM suggests consumers are prioritizing essential trips over discretionary shopping. If that pattern persists, retail-and-recreation mobility will continue to weaken over the next four weeks as spending shifts away from mall and leisure visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -11.6 to -22.9 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive but eased to 1.9
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and RETAIL_REC becomes less negative over the next 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.
